project.title: Proteomics of E. coli extracellular vesicles
project.projectDescription: Escherichia coli A0 34/86 (EcO83) is a probiotic bacterium that is used in newborns to prevent nosocomial infections and diarrhoea. Mechanistically, EcO83 enhances innate immunity by inducing key inflammatory cytokines in vitro, and when administered intranasally, it modulates the recruitment of cells to the lung. This study investigates the immunomodulatory effects of EcO83-derived extracellular vesicles (EcO83-EVs) as a safer alternative to live bacteria. We isolated, purified, and characterised EcO83-EVs following the MISEV guidelines. The proteomics data of the EVs were compared with the proteomics data of cell extracts of the EcO83.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Proteomics analyses of EcO83-EVs and EcO83 cell lysates were performed as previously described [PMID: 37864211]. Briefly, 20 μg of protein was dissolved in Laemmli buffer, and run on the SDS-PAGE. Reduced cysteine residues were blocked with iodoacetamide (Sigma Aldrich, USA) and proteins were digested by trypsin (Sigma Aldrich) in the gel. Peptides were purified on PepClean™ C18 Spin Columns (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and dried using a Speedvac, miVac Duo Concentrator (Genevac, UK). Peptides were analyzed using a nano-LC (Easy-nLC 1200, Thermo Fisher Scientific)-tandem-MS (Q-Exactive HF-X Hybrid Quadrupole Orbitrap, Thermo Fisher Scientific).
project.dataProcessingProtocol: MaxQuant (v1.5.3.30) was used to identify and quantify proteins against the E. coli K12 database (https://www.uniprot.org/). Matching between runs was performed and iBAQ intensities were used for quantification and processed in Perseus v2.0.11. Proteins were filtered with a permutation-based false discovery rate (FDR). EcO83-EVs were annotated as 2-1, 2-2 and 2-3 and the EcO83 lysates as 2-4, 2-5, 2-6.
